changes: Group aggregate tasks within a child memory scope and transfer grouped output allocations into the aggregate input lifetime.
Admit canonical grouping key formatting through the shared stable-data key helper, plus directory entries, detached task payloads, range copies, result slots and sort workspace.
Release grouping keys and lookup directory after grouping; release all child allocations immediately when grouping fails.
Use canonical data-key semantics for partition/property ordering and detach complete task descriptors.

validation.budget_test: Group 20 fragmented tasks under 128 KiB, assert retained capacity, reject peak-minus-one and return to zero without requiring caller scope disposal.

tradeoffs: Admission and stable-key formatting cost more CPU than the unadmitted intermediate implementation. At 4000 ranges this run measured 45.3 ms versus 196.7 ms for the prior repeated-merge baseline; the earlier 1.09 ms unadmitted measurement is not current performance.
Removed overlapping range objects remain conservatively charged until grouped task lifetime ends.
Native sort/runtime bookkeeping is represented by conservative accounting charges, not an exact JS heap cap.
remaining: Broader legacy/spill/resume allocation integration and mixed-job 64/128 MiB acceptance remain open.
Refresh full release gates after this implementation.
